intro_en: In this lesson you learn to give your own opinion with 〜と思います. You also learn to tell what another person said with 〜と言います. You can repeat their exact words, or just give the meaning. You will also meet でしょう？. It means "isn’t it?" and asks the listener to agree. 〜で〜があります tells where an event happens. について means "about". 〜ので gives a reason in a soft way. Japanese と works just like Tamil "என்று" (that / saying). So this lesson should feel very easy for you.

g21-1.explanation_en: Use 〜と思います to give your opinion or a guess. In Tamil you say "நாளை மழை பெய்யும் என்று நினைக்கிறேன்" (I think it will rain tomorrow). The order is: full sentence + "என்று" + "நினைக்கிறேன்". Japanese uses exactly the same order: sentence + と + 思います. Here と is the same as Tamil "என்று". The sentence before と must be in the plain form (普通形). This is the short, casual form from Lesson 20. For example: 降る、降らない、降った、難しい、難しかった. Nouns and な-adjectives take だ: 先生だと思います、大切だと思います. To say "I don’t think so", there are two ways. You can put the "not" inside: 〜ないと思います. Or you can put it outside: 〜とは思いません. For N5, the first way is enough. To ask what someone thinks, say 〜についてどう思いますか.
g21-1.tamil_parallel_en: "நாளை மழை பெய்யும் என்று நினைக்கிறேன்" (I think it will rain tomorrow) = 明日は雨が降ると思います. The order is the same in both languages. Sentence + "என்று" (と) + "நினைக்கிறேன்" (思います).
g21-1.formation_en: Verb or い-adjective (plain form) + と 思います ； Noun or な-adjective + だ + と 思います ； "Not": 〜ない + と 思います
g21-1.pitfalls_en: A common mistake is to put the ます-form before と: ×降りますと思います → ○降ると思います. Don’t forget だ after a noun: ×先生と思います → ○先生だと思います.

g21-2.explanation_en: Use 言います (to say) to tell what someone said. There are two ways. (1) Exact words: put the exact words inside 「 」. Then add と言いました: 田中さんは「おはよう」と言いました. (2) Just the meaning: give the meaning of what was said in the plain form (the short form). Then add と言いました: 先生は明日テストがあると言いました. Here too, と is the same as Tamil "என்று". In Tamil we say "அவர் நாளை தேர்வு இருக்கிறது என்று சொன்னார்" (he said there is a test tomorrow). To ask "How do you say X in Japanese?", use 「X」は日本語で何と言いますか. When you pass on what someone said, you can also use 言っていました. It means "was saying" or "had said".
g21-2.tamil_parallel_en: "ஆசிரியர் 'நாளை தேர்வு' என்று சொன்னார்" (the teacher said "test tomorrow") = 先生は「明日テストです」と言いました. Tamil "என்று" and Japanese と do the same job. Both join the quoted words to the verb "say".
g21-2.formation_en: 「exact words」 + と 言います ； plain form + と 言います ； 「X」は 〜語で 何と 言いますか
g21-2.pitfalls_en: The person who speaks is marked with は. The person you speak to is marked with に: 田中さんは私に…と言いました. Don’t mix up 言う (to say) and 話す (to talk). と does not come before 話す.

g21-3.explanation_en: Say でしょう？ with your voice going up at the end. Use it to check something when you expect the listener to agree. It means "isn’t it?" or "right?". It is like Tamil "இந்தச் சாப்பாடு சுவையாக இருக்கிறது, இல்லையா?" (this food is tasty, isn’t it?). It is also like "நீ நாளை வருவாய்தானே?" (you’re coming tomorrow, right?). Put the plain form (the short form) before でしょう. Nouns and な-adjectives do not take だ: 日本人でしょう？、静かでしょう？. ね from Lesson 4 also asks the listener to agree. But でしょう fits best when the listener already knows the answer.
g21-3.tamil_parallel_en: "இந்தச் சாப்பாடு சுவையாக இருக்கிறது, இல்லையா?" (this food is tasty, isn’t it?) = この料理、おいしいでしょう？ The Tamil ending "இல்லையா?" / "-தானே?" does the same job as でしょう？.
g21-3.formation_en: Verb or い-adjective (plain form) + でしょう？ ； Noun or な-adjective (no だ) + でしょう？
g21-3.pitfalls_en: Don’t put だ after a noun: ×日本人だでしょう → ○日本人でしょう. If your voice goes down at the end, でしょう becomes a guess. Then it means "it is probably so". To ask the listener to agree, your voice must go up.

g21-4.explanation_en: In Lesson 10, you used に for the place where a thing is. For example, "there is a book on the desk": 机の上に本があります. Events are different. A party, a test, a class or a festival is an event. For the place where an event happens, use で: 学校でパーティーがあります. It is like Tamil "பள்ளியில் பார்ட்டி இருக்கிறது/நடக்கிறது" (there is / will be a party at school). Why で? In Lesson 6 you learned that で marks the place where an action happens. An event is an action, so it takes で. Put the time of the event first, with に: 土曜日に学校でパーティーがあります.
g21-4.tamil_parallel_en: "சனிக்கிழமை பள்ளியில் பார்ட்டி இருக்கிறது" (there is a party at school on Saturday) = 土曜日に学校でパーティーがあります. Place + "-இல்" (で) + event + が + あります.
g21-4.formation_en: time に + place で + event が あります ； "Not": 〜が ありません
g21-4.pitfalls_en: Tamil speakers often use に for events by mistake. In Tamil, both places use "-இல்" (in/at). ×学校にパーティーがあります → ○学校でパーティーがあります. Only the place where a thing is takes に.

g21-5.explanation_en: To say what you talk, write or think "about", put について after the noun. It matches Tamil "-ஐப் பற்றி" (about) exactly. For example: 日本の食べ物について (ஜப்பானிய உணவைப் பற்றி, about Japanese food). Learn について as one word. Nothing like の or を comes before it. Verbs like these often come after it: 話します、書きます、質問があります、どう思いますか. To use "about" to describe a noun, like "a book about...", use についての + noun: 日本についての本.
g21-5.tamil_parallel_en: "பயணத்தைப் பற்றி நண்பனுடன் பேசினேன்" (I talked with my friend about the trip) = 旅行について友達と話しました. Noun + "பற்றி" (about) = noun + について.
g21-5.formation_en: Noun + について + verb (話します / 書きます / 聞きます / 思います)
g21-5.pitfalls_en: Don’t put を before について: ×旅行をについて → ○旅行について. Using only に to mean "about" is also wrong.

g21-6.explanation_en: When one sentence ends, you can start the next one with "but". Use でも or しかし. It is like Tamil "ஜப்பானிய மொழி கடினம். ஆனால் சுவாரசியமானது." (Japanese is hard. But it is interesting.). Use でも when you speak, with friends and in everyday talk. Use しかし in essays, the news and formal speeches. Both stand alone at the start of a sentence, followed by 、. 〜が、〜 (Lesson 8) and 〜けど (Lesson 20) are different. They join onto the end of the sentence before. でも and しかし start a new sentence.
g21-6.tamil_parallel_en: "இந்தக் கடை விலை அதிகம். ஆனால் சுவையாக இருக்கும்." (This shop is expensive. But it is tasty.) = この店は高いです。でも、おいしいです。 Tamil "ஆனால்" (but) starts the second sentence. It matches でも / しかし.
g21-6.formation_en: Sentence 1。 + でも、 / しかし、 + Sentence 2。
g21-6.pitfalls_en: Don’t put でも in the middle of a sentence to mean "but": ×高いですでも、 → ○高いですが、 or ○高いです。でも、.

g21-7.explanation_en: In Lesson 9 you learned 〜から to give a reason. 〜ので does the same job. But it sounds softer and more polite. It shows the reason as a natural cause: "because of this, that happened". It matches Tamil "-ஆதலால்", "-என்பதால்" (because / since). For example: 時間がないので (நேரம் இல்லாததால், because there is no time). Put the plain form (the short form) before ので. After nouns and な-adjectives, use なので: 風邪なので、下手なので. When you say sorry, say no, or ask for something, ので is more polite. The ます/です form can come before から. But before ので, you normally use the plain form.
g21-7.tamil_parallel_en: "நேரம் இல்லாததால் டாக்ஸியில் போகிறேன்" (because there is no time, I will go by taxi) = 時間がないので、タクシーで行きます. Reason + "-ஆதலால்" (ので) + result. The order is the same as Tamil.
g21-7.formation_en: Verb or い-adjective (plain form) + ので、〜 ； Noun or な-adjective + なので、〜
g21-7.pitfalls_en: Saying だので after a noun is wrong: ×風邪だので → ○風邪なので. A request ("please do") can come after ので. But for an invitation like "let’s do" (ましょう), から fits better.

items.L21-q01: 新聞 = しんぶん (செய்தித்தாள், newspaper). Here 聞 is read ぶん. It is not the きく reading from 聞く (to listen). しんもん is a trap. It mixes the word up with 質問 (しつもん).
items.L21-q02: 声 = こえ (குரல், voice). ごえ has こ changed to ご. That change only happens inside longer words. On its own, the word is always こえ. おと is a different word. It means "sound".
items.L21-q03: 言葉 = ことば (வார்த்தை, word). Here 葉 is read ば, with the two dots (゛). ことは, without the dots, is wrong. In こどば, と has wrongly changed to ど.
items.L21-q04: おなじ = 同じ (ஒரே, same). 回 (かい, time) and 国 (くに, country) look like 同. But 同 has one line and a 口 inside.
items.L21-q05: しつもん = 質問 (கேள்வி, question). 問 (もん) has a 口 inside. 門 (gate) has no 口 inside. That is the trap in 質門. 貿 and 資 look like 質, but they are different kanji.
items.L21-q06: To say "no thanks, that’s enough" politely, people say いいえ、結構です (けっこうです) (வேண்டாம், போதும், no thank you). べんり (handy) and たいせつ (important) don’t fit here.
items.L21-q07: To say "A is different from B", use AはBと違います (வேறுபடுகிறது, is different). 答えます (to answer) and 始まります (to begin) don’t fit the meaning here.
items.L21-q08: 大勢の人 = (நிறையப் பேர், a lot of people). 大切 (important), 大変 (hard) and 大丈夫 (all right) also start with 大. But only 大勢 talks about a number of people.
items.L21-q09: The class starts at nine and ends at twelve. So use 始まります (தொடங்குகிறது, starts). 止まります (stops) is for a car or a machine stopping. It is not used for a class.
items.L21-q10: To ask "why didn’t you come?", use なぜ (ஏன், why). It is the same as どうして. いつ (when) doesn’t fit. The answer 昨日 (yesterday) is already in the sentence.
items.L21-q11: You watch ニュース (செய்தி, news) on TV. You listen to the ラジオ (radio). You can’t watch the radio on TV. 声 (voice) is also something you hear.
items.L21-q12: "A student at the same school" means they both study at one school. The first choice, 違います (is different), means the opposite. 先生 (teacher) is not a student.
items.L21-q13: The exact words 「明日休みます」 (I will take tomorrow off) mean the same as 明日来ないと言いました (நாளை வர மாட்டேன் என்று சொன்னார், he said he won’t come tomorrow). 来る and 働く give the opposite meaning. 昨日 is the wrong time.
items.L21-q14: "I don’t understand the meaning" means "I don’t know this word" (知りません, தெரியாது). 難しくない (not difficult) means the opposite. よく使います (I use it often) doesn’t fit a word you don’t know.
items.L21-q15: The plain form (普通形, the short form) must come before と思います: 降ると思います (பெய்யும் என்று நினைக்கிறேன், I think it will fall). Putting the ます-form (降ります) there is wrong. Tamil learners often make this mistake.
items.L21-q16: When a noun comes before と思います, you need だ in between: 先生だと思います. です is the polite form. It doesn’t come before と. な is only used when a な-adjective comes before a noun.
items.L21-q17: To join someone’s words to 言いました, use と. It is the same as Tamil "என்று". を is a trap. It comes from translating the Tamil "-ஐ" in "சொன்னதை" (what was said) word for word.
items.L21-q18: After a noun, ので becomes なので: 風邪なので (சளி என்பதால், because I have a cold). だので does not exist. With から, you would need 風邪ですから or 風邪だから. 風邪から alone changes the meaning to "from a cold".
items.L21-q19: A party is an event. The place where an event happens takes で. に is only for the place where a thing is (公園に木があります).
items.L21-q20: "About" = について (பற்றி). Learn it as one word. をついて and のついて are wrong.
items.L21-q21: The plain form (short form) 行く + でしょう？ = (போகிறீர்கள்தானே?, you’re going, right?). 行くですか is a wrong mix. It should be 行きますか. Forms like 行くません and 行くましょう don’t exist.
items.L21-q22: 田中さんは パーティーに 来ないと 思います。 — (தனாகா பார்ட்டிக்கு வர மாட்டார் என்று நினைக்கிறேன், I think Tanaka won’t come to the party). The order is: 来ない (the short "not" form) + と + 思います. 来ない goes in the star position.
items.L21-q23: 明日 学校で 日本語の テストが あります。 — First comes the place where the event happens (で). Next comes which test (日本語の テストが). あります comes at the end. テストが goes in the star position.
items.L21-q24: 時間が ないので、駅まで タクシーで 行きます。 — The reason (ないので) comes first. Then "how far" (駅まで), then "how" (タクシーで). The verb comes at the end. タクシーで goes in the star position.
items.L21-q25: ［1］ After someone’s exact words, use と to join them to 言いました. ［2］ My friend said it is "difficult". But I think it is "not difficult". The opinions are opposite, so use でも (ஆனால், but). そして and それから mean "and then". They just continue the same idea. ［3］ The plain form (short form) 行く must come before と思います. 行きます is wrong.
